title: Arakhin 14
description: Why the chapter’s mishna speaks only of Jews, then three of its cases where the Torah fixes the sum and others are assessed: the ancestral field redeemed at fifty shekels per kor of barley seed, with Rav Huna’s trees, Rav Pappa’s rocky fields and Rabbi Eliezer’s purchased field; the forewarned ox that killed a slave; and the rapist and seducer.
topics: 🗣️ Rav: it is forbidden to say “How beautiful is this gentile”
🌾 Sands or the orchards of Sebastia: fifty silver shekels for an area for sowing a kor of barley
🌳 Rav Huna: trees by their value, then the land; Rav Naḥman’s three objections
👨‍👦 A field bought from one’s father: when does it count as ancestral?
🪨 Rav Pappa on rocky fields and on trees, consecrated or sold
➕ Does a purchased field add a fifth? Rava and the “two verses that come as one”
🐂 The forewarned ox: thirty sela for any slave, a freeman’s price, full damage for injury
⚖️ The rapist and seducer: fifty sela for all, and humiliation and degradation besides

a1.he: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָמַשְׁמַע לַן, כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָסוּר לָאָדָם שֶׁיֹּאמַר ״כַּמָּה נָאֶה גּוֹי זֶה״.

a2.he: וְלִיתְנֵי ״אֶת הַנָּאֶה שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֶת הַכָּעוּר שֶׁבַּגּוֹיִם״! בְּחַד אוּמָּה קָמַיְירֵי, בִּתְרֵי אוּמֵּי לָא מַיְירֵי.

a3.he: וְלָא? וְהָא קָתָנֵי: הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבַּכְּהוּנָּה וְאֶת הַקְּטַנָּה שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל! הָתָם חַד אוּמָּה הוּא, אֶלָּא מִקְדָּישׁ הוּא דְּקַדִּישִׁי כֹּהֲנִים טְפֵי.

a4.he: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, אַיְּידֵי דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְמִתְנֵי סֵיפָא ״שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה״, דִּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא דְּמַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ, בְּגוֹי לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ, דְּלָאו בְּנֵי אֲחוּזָּה נִינְהוּ, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קָתָנֵי לַהּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.

a5.he: מַתְנִי׳ בִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר, כֵּיצַד? אֶחָד הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בְּחוֹלַת הַמָּחוֹז, וְאֶחָד הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּפַּרְדֵּיסוֹת סְבַסְטֵי, נוֹתֵן זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף, וּבִשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה נוֹתֵן אֶת שׇׁוְויוֹ.

a6.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה וְאֶחָד שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, מָה בֵּין שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה לִשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה? שֶׁבִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה הוּא נוֹתֵן חוֹמֶשׁ, וּבִשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה אֵינוֹ נוֹתֵן חוֹמֶשׁ.

a7.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הִקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֶה מְלֵיאָה אִילָנוֹת, כְּשֶׁהוּא פּוֹדָן — פּוֹדֶה אִילָנוֹת בְּשׇׁוְויָן, וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה קַרְקַע בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף. אַלְמָא קָסָבַר רַב הוּנָא: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ — בְּעַיִן יָפָה מַקְדִּישׁ.

a8.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא: אֶחָד הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בְּחוֹלַת הַמָּחוֹז, וְאֶחָד הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בְּפַרְדֵּיסוֹת סְבַסְטֵי, נוֹתֵן בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רְאוּיָה לְפַרְדֵּיסוֹת קָאָמֵינָא.

a9.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: ״בֵּית זֶרַע״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בֵּית זֶרַע, שְׂדֵה גְּפָנִים וּשְׂדֵה קָנִים וּשְׂדֵה אִילָנוֹת מִנַּיִן?

a10.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״שָׂדֶה״ מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכָא נָמֵי פּוֹדֶה וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה.

a11.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: הִקְדִּישׁ שְׁלֹשָׁה אִילָנוֹת מִמַּטַּע עֲשָׂרָה לְבֵית סְאָה — הֲרֵי זֶה הִקְדִּישׁ אֶת הַקַּרְקַע וְאֶת הָאִילָנוֹת שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם, כְּשֶׁהוּא פּוֹדֶה — פּוֹדֶה בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף.

a12.he: פָּחוֹת מִיכֵּן, אוֹ יָתֵר עַל כֵּן, אוֹ שֶׁהִקְדִּישָׁן בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה — הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא הִקְדִּישׁ לֹא אֶת הַקַּרְקַע וְלֹא אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם.

a13.he: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּישׁ אִילָנוֹתָיו, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישׁ קַרְקַע, כְּשֶׁהוּא פּוֹדֶה — פּוֹדֶה אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת בְּשׇׁוְויֵהֶן, וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה קַרְקַע: בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף!

a14.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכָא נָמֵי פּוֹדֶה וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה, הָא מִדְּסֵיפָא פּוֹדֶה וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה, מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא לָא!

a15.he: אֶלָּא, הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דְּאָמַר: מַקְדִּישׁ בְּעַיִן רָעָה מַקְדִּישׁ. דְּתַנְיָא: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה — הִקְדִּישׁ אֶת כּוּלָּהּ. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לֹא הִקְדִּישׁ אֶלָּא חָרוּב הַמּוּרְכָּב וְסַדַּן הַשִּׁקְמָה.

a16.he: אִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּישׁ אִילָנוֹתָיו וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישׁ קַרְקַע, כְּשֶׁהוּא פּוֹדֶה — פּוֹדֶה אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת בְּשׇׁוְויֵהֶן, וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף.

a17.he: וְאִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — לֵיזִיל בָּתַר פִּדְיוֹן, וְלִיפְרְקוּ אַגַּב אַרְעַיְיהוּ, דְּהָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָזֵיל בָּתַר פִּדְיוֹן!

a18.he: דְּתַנְיָא: מִנַּיִן לְלוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת אָבִיו, מִנַּיִן שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִם אֶת שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״.

a19.he: שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁרְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.

a20.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לַלּוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו, וּמֵת אָבִיו, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ, מִנַּיִן שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה?

b1.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִם אֶת שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּתוֹ״ — שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁהִיא שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה.

b2.he: אִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת אָב — שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה הָוְיָא. מַאי טַעְמָא? אִי מִשּׁוּם קְרָא — קְרָא לְכִדְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הוּא דַּאֲתָא!

b3.he: אֶלָּא לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָזֵיל בָּתַר פִּדְיוֹן?

b4.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קְרָא אַשְׁכַּחוּ וּדְרוּשׁ.

b5.he: אִם כֵּן, לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא: ״אִם אֶת שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״, מַאי ״מִשְּׂדֵה״ — שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה.

b6.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִקְדִּישׁ טְרָשִׁין — פּוֹדָן בְּשׇׁוְויָן, מַאי טַעְמָא? ״בֵּית זֶרַע״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהָנֵי לָאו בְּנֵי זְרִיעָה נִינְהוּ.

b7.he: לֹא גְּאָלָן — יוֹצְאִין [לַכֹּהֲנִים] בַּיּוֹבֵל, מַאי טַעְמָא? ״שָׂדֶה״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, כֹּל דְּהוּ.

b8.he: מָכַר טְרָשִׁין — נִגְאָלִין פָּחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים, מַאי טַעְמָא? ״מִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי תְבוּאוֹת״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהַאי לָאו בְּנֵי תְבוּאָה נִינְהוּ. לֹא גְּאָלָן — (חוֹזֶרֶת) [חוֹזְרִין] לַבְּעָלִים בַּיּוֹבֵל, מַאי טַעְמָא? ״וְשָׁב לַאֲחוּזָּתוֹ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהַאי נָמֵי אֲחוּזָּה הִיא.

b9.he: הִקְדִּישׁ אִילָנוֹת — (פּוֹדֶה) [פּוֹדָן] בְּשׇׁוְויֵהֶן, מַאי טַעְמָא? ״בֵּית זֶרַע״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא אִילָנוֹת. לֹא גְּאָלָן — אֵין יוֹצְאִין לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל, ״וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא אִילָנוֹת.

b10.he: מָכַר אִילָנוֹת — אֵין נִגְאָלִין פָּחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים, מַאי טַעְמָא? ״שְׁנֵי תְבוּאוֹת״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהָנֵי בְּנֵי תְבוּאוֹת נִינְהוּ. לֹא גְּאָלָן — אֵין חוֹזֶרֶת לַבְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל, מַאי טַעְמָא? ״וְשָׁב לַאֲחוּזָּתוֹ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא אִילָנוֹת.

b11.he: אָמַר מָר: הִקְדִּישׁ אִילָנוֹת — (פּוֹדֶה) [פּוֹדָן] בְּשׇׁוְויָן. אַמַּאי? וְלִיקְדְּשׁוּ אַגַּב אַרְעַיְיהוּ, וְלִיפְרְקוּהָ אַגַּב אַרְעַיְיהוּ!

b12.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אִילָנוֹת אַקְדֵּישׁ, אַרְעָא לָא אַקְדֵּישׁ — וְהָאָמְרִי נְהַרְדָּעֵי: מַאן דִּמְזַבֵּן לֵיהּ דִּקְלָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ, קָנֵי לֵיהּ מִשִּׁיפּוּלָא וְעַד תְּהוֹמָא! לָאו מִי אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ: בְּבָא מֵחֲמַת טַעֲנָה!

b13.he: שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה נוֹתֵן שׇׁוְויוֹ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בְּמִכְסַת״ — מַה בָּא לִלְמוֹד? לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״זֶרַע חֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף״, יָכוֹל אַף שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה כֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מִכְסַת״.

b14.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״וְחִשַּׁב״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״וְחִשַּׁב״, מָה לְהַלָּן דָּבָר קָצוּב, אַף כָּאן דָּבָר קָצוּב.

b15.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבָּנַן אִית לְהוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, וּמַפְּקִין לֵיהּ לְחוֹמֶשׁ, אוֹ דִלְמָא לֵית לְהוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, וְלֵית לְהוּ לְחוֹמֶשׁ?

b16.he: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא לֵית לְהוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, מִדְּגַלִּי רַחֲמָנָא חוֹמֶשׁ גַּבֵּי שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה וְגַבֵּי מַקְדִּישׁ בֵּיתוֹ, הָווּ לֵיהּ שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד, וְכׇל שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִין.

b17.he: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְלַמְּדִין, מִדְּגַלִּי רַחֲמָנָא חוֹמֶשׁ בְּמַעֲשֵׂר, בִּבְהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה, וּבִבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה — הָוֵה לֵיהּ טוּבָא, וְאֵין מְלַמְּדִין.

b18.he: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרָבָא, וְלָא מִטַּעְמֵיהּ. תַּנְיָא: ״בְּמִכְסַת הָעֶרְכְּךָ״ — הִקִּישׁוֹ הַכָּתוּב לַעֲרָכִין, מָה עֲרָכִין אֵין מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ, אַף שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה אֵין מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.

b19.he: מַתְנִי׳ בְּשׁוֹר הַמּוּעָד שֶׁהֵמִית אֶת הָעֶבֶד לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר, כֵּיצַד? אֶחָד שֶׁהֵמִית אֶת הַנָּאֶה שֶׁבַּעֲבָדִים וְאֶת הַכָּעוּר שֶׁבָּעֲבָדִים — נוֹתֵן שְׁלֹשִׁים סֶלַע. הֵמִית בֶּן חוֹרִין — נוֹתֵן שׇׁוְויוֹ. חָבַל בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה — נוֹתֵן נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם.

b20.he: גְּמָ׳ בְּמוּעָד — אִין, בְּתָם — לָא. לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אַף תָּם שֶׁחָבַל בָּאָדָם מְשַׁלֵּם בַּמּוֹתָר נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם.

b21.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ תָּם נָמֵי, וְאַיְּידֵי דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְמִתְנֵי סֵיפָא ״הֵמִית עֶבֶד״ ״הֵמִית בֶּן חוֹרִין״, דִּבְמוּעָד הוּא דְּמַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ, בְּתָם לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קָתָנֵי מוּעָד.

b22.he: מַתְנִי׳ בָּאוֹנֵס וּבַמְפַתֶּה לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר, כֵּיצַד? אֶחָד שֶׁאָנַס וּפִיתָּה אֶת גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבַּכְּהוּנָּה וְאֶת הַקְּטַנָּה שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל — נוֹתֵן חֲמִשִּׁים סְלָעִים, וְהַבּוֹשֶׁת וְהַפְּגָם — הַכֹּל לְפִי הַמְבַיֵּישׁ וְהַמִּתְבַּיֵּישׁ.

b23.he: גְּמָ׳ אַמַּאי? אֵימָא: ״חֲמִשִּׁים סְלָעִים״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא מִכֹּל מִילֵּי!

b24.he: אָמַר רַב זְעֵירָא: יֹאמְרוּ, בָּעַל בַּת מְלָכִים חֲמִשִּׁים, בָּעַל בַּת הֶדְיוֹטוֹת חֲמִשִּׁים?

b25.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי הָכִי, גַּבֵּי עֶבֶד נָמֵי, יֹאמְרוּ: עֶבֶד נוֹקֵב מַרְגָּלִית — שְׁלֹשִׁים, עֶבֶד עוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֵׂה מַחַט — שְׁלֹשִׁים? אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב זְעֵירָא:

messages.text: Continued from 13b: the mishna spoke of valuating the most attractive and most unsightly among the Jewish people. The Gemara answered that it can follow Rabbi Meir, since a gentile, too, is valuated at the fixed sum. But…
Gemara
…by not mentioning gentiles, the mishna teaches us another matter in passing, in accordance with the statement that Rav Yehuda says that Rav says.

notes.he: דלא תנא את הנאה שבכנענים לפי שאסור להזכיר שם נוי על כנעני כדרב יהודה דכתיב (דברים ז) לא תחנם לא תתן להם חן:
notes.en: It teaches us another matter in passing: that it did not teach “the most attractive among the gentiles,” because it is forbidden to apply a term of beauty to a gentile, in accordance with Rav Yehuda, as it is written: “Nor show mercy to them [lo teḥonnem]” (Deuteronomy 7:2), [read as] do not grant them grace [ḥen].

messages.text: It is prohibited for a person to say: How beautiful is this gentile.

notes.dh: [אסור לאדם לומר כמה נאה עובד כוכבים זה
notes.he: משום שנאמר לא תחנם לא תתן להם חן]:
notes.en: [It is forbidden for a person to say: How beautiful is this gentile, because it is stated: “Nor show mercy to them” (Deuteronomy 7:2): do not grant them grace.]

messages.text: But if this is the only reason that a gentile is not mentioned, let the mishna teach: In the case of one who took a vow of valuation to donate the fixed value of the most attractive among the Jewish people and the most unsightly among the gentiles, he gives the fixed payment of fifty sela to the Temple treasury.
The tanna prefers to deal with one nation, i.e., Jews, and does not wish to deal with two nations, Jews and gentiles.

And does the mishna not deal with two nations? But isn’t it taught in a mishna (14b): One who raped or seduced a young woman, whether she is the most prominent in the priesthood or the lowliest among the Israelites, gives the payment of fifty sela, the fine stated in the Torah. Priests and Israelites are two distinct groups of people, analogous to Jews and gentiles.

notes.he: גבי אונס ומפתה:
notes.en: But isn’t it taught: with regard to the rapist and the seducer.

notes.dh: את הקטנה שבישראל ואת הגדולה שבכהונה
notes.he: אלמא בתרתי אומי קא מיירי:
notes.en: The lowliest among the Israelites and the most prominent in the priesthood: evidently it does deal with two nations.

messages.text: In that mishna there it is one nation, as although there are two groups they are both part of the Jewish people. It is only that the priests have greater sanctity than Israelites.

And if you wish, say instead that since the mishna wants to teach the case of an ancestral field in the latter clause, which you find in the case of Jews, but you do not find with regard to gentiles, as they are unfit to have ancestral land in Eretz Yisrael, it is due to this reason that the mishna teaches only cases that involve the Jewish people.

notes.he: דין שדה אחוזה שיהא פודהו בחמשים שקל כסף אלא בשויו דלאו בני אחוזה בארץ ישראל נינהו:
notes.en: With a gentile you do not find it: the law of an ancestral field, that one redeems it for fifty silver shekels and not at its value, for they are not people with ancestral holdings in Eretz Yisrael.

notes.he: משום דלאו בני אחוזה נינהו ואע"ג דאמרינן (קדושין דף יז:) עובד כוכבים יורש אביו דבר תורה מ"מ לא היה להם אחוזה בארץ ודין זה לא שייך כי אם בא"י דמצוה היא התלויה בארץ ועובד כוכבים אין לו נחלה בארץ:
notes.en: With a gentile you do not find it: because they are not people with ancestral holdings. And even though we say (Kiddushin 17b) that a gentile inherits his father by Torah law, nevertheless they had no ancestral holding in the land, and this law applies only in Eretz Yisrael, for it is a mitzva dependent on the land, and a gentile has no inheritance in the land.

notes.he: דלאו בני אחוזה נינהו דעובד כוכבים לא קני (גופא) [שדה] ועוד שאין לו שאר אב ואין יורש את אביו:
notes.en: For they are not people with ancestral holdings [the editor suggests adding: in Eretz Yisrael], for a gentile does not acquire [the field itself]; and furthermore, he has no paternal kin and does not inherit his father. [The editor notes: see Kiddushin 17b, that a gentile inherits his father by Torah law, and so Tosafot here; this needs examination.]

messages.text: Mishna
There are halakhot with regard to an ancestral field that are lenient and others that are stringent. How so?

Both one who consecrates an ancestral field in the low-quality sands of the areas surrounding the city and one who consecrates the high-quality orchards of Sebastia gives a redemption payment of fifty silver shekels for every area that he consecrated that is fit for sowing a kor of barley (Leviticus 27:16).

verse.he: וְאִם ׀ מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ לְפִי זַרְעוֹ זֶרַע חֹמֶר שְׂעֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף׃
verse.en: If anyone consecrates to GOD a land-holding, its assessment shall be in accordance with its seed requirement: fifty shekels of silver to a ḥomer of barley seed.

notes.he: שדה בחולת המחוז סביבות עיר שאינה חשובה כ"כ מפני מדרס הרגלים. חולת סביבות כמו מחול הכרם (כלאים פ"ד מ"א). (ל"א) מחוז עיר. ל"א מחוז שם מקום שלא היו שדותיו חשובין:
notes.en: Mishna. Both one who consecrates: a field in the sands of the maḥoz, around a city, which is not so valuable because of the trampling of feet. Ḥulat [means] the surroundings, like “the open space [meḥol] of a vineyard” (Kilayim 4:1). (Another version:) maḥoz [means] a city. Another version: Maḥoz is the name of a place whose fields were not valuable.

notes.he: כרמים של אותו מקום ומעולים הם מאוד:
notes.en: The orchards of Sebastia: the vineyards of that place, and they are of very high quality.

notes.he: מי שפודה אותם בין בעלים בין אדם אחר בבית זרע חומר שעורים חמשים שקל כסף אם תחלת היובל היה ואם לא מגרע לפי השנים שעברו סלע ופונדיון לשנה כדכתיב קרא:
notes.en: Gives: whoever redeems them, whether the owner or another person, [gives] fifty silver shekels for an area for sowing a ḥomer of barley, if it was at the beginning of the Jubilee [cycle]; and if not, he deducts according to the years that have passed, a sela and a pundeyon for each year, as the verse writes.

notes.he: מתני' בחולת המחוז היינו שדה שסמוכה למחוז העיר שדורכין אותה בני אדם ועוד כיון שסמוכה לעיר ועומדת בקמתה רואין אותה בני אדם ונותנין בה עין רעה ואינו עושה פירות כ"כ:
notes.en: Mishna. In the sands of the maḥoz: that is, a field near the city’s maḥoz, which people trample; and furthermore, since it is near the city and stands with its standing grain, people see it and cast an evil eye on it, and it does not produce so much fruit.

notes.he: שבאותו מקום שהן מעולות הרבה כשהוא פודה נותן בין בזו ובין בזו נ' שקל:
notes.en: The orchards of Sebastia: which in that place are of very high quality. When he redeems, he gives fifty shekels, whether for this or for that.

messages.text: And with regard to a purchased field that one consecrates, he gives its value as redemption, a sum that can be more or less than fifty shekels for every area required for sowing one kor of barley.
With regard to both a purchased field and an ancestral field, one gives a redemption payment of fifty silver shekels for every area required for sowing a kor of barley that he consecrated.

notes.he: דכולהו מיפרקי בנ' שקלים:
notes.en: Both an ancestral field etc.: for all of them are redeemed for fifty shekels.

messages.text: What, then, is the difference between an ancestral field and a purchased field? The difference is that in the case of an ancestral field one gives an additional payment of one-fifth, but in the case of a purchased field one does not give an additional payment of one-fifth.

notes.he: אם בעלים פודין אותה מוסיפין חומש על החמישים כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:י״ט) ואם גאל יגאל את השדה המקדיש וגו':
notes.en: An ancestral field: if the owner redeems it, one adds a fifth to the fifty, as it is written: “And if he that sanctified the field will redeem it” etc. (Leviticus 27:19).

notes.he: כדמפרש בגמ':
notes.en: And with a purchased field one does not give a fifth: as is explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: Gemara

In a case where one consecrated a field full of trees, when he redeems the trees and field, he redeems the trees according to their value, and then redeems the land according to the fixed formula, by which an area required for the sowing of a kor of barley seed is redeemed for fifty silver shekels.

Evidently Rav Huna holds that when a person consecrates, he consecrates generously. In this case he consecrated the trees and the land separately, so that he would have to redeem them each separately, rather than the trees being redeemed as part of the land.

notes.he: אילנות לבד וקרקע לבד ולא שיפדה אילנות אגב קרקע:
notes.en: Gemara. He consecrates generously: the trees by themselves and the land by itself, and not that the trees are redeemed along with the land.

notes.he: והקדיש את האלנות לדמיהן [לבד וחוזר ופודה קרקע כו']:
notes.en: Gemara. He consecrates generously: and he consecrated the trees for their value [by themselves, and then he redeems the land, etc.].

messages.text: Both one who consecrates an ancestral field in the low-quality sands of the areas surrounding the city and one who consecrates the high-quality orchards of Sebastia gives a redemption payment of fifty silver shekels for every area required for sowing a kor of barley that he consecrated. This indicates that when one consecrates orchards he does not redeem the land and the trees separately.
messages.lead: Rav Naḥman raised an objection to Rav Huna from the mishna:

notes.he: היינו כרמים נטועים וקתני חמשים שקל אלמא נפדין אילנות אגב קרקע:
notes.en: Orchards: these are planted vineyards, and it teaches fifty shekels; evidently the trees are redeemed along with the land.

notes.he: פרדיסות משמע דאית בה אילנות וקתני נותן [בבית] זרע חומר שעורים נ' שקל אלמא אינו צריך לפדות את האילנות בפני עצמן:
notes.en: Orchards implies that it has trees, and it teaches that he gives fifty shekels [for an area of] sowing a ḥomer of barley; evidently he need not redeem the trees by themselves.

messages.text: @Rav Naḥman The mishna is speaking of land that is suitable for orchards but does not actually have trees planted on it.

notes.he: ואינה נטועה:
notes.en: Suitable: but not planted.

notes.he: ולא דאית ביה אילנות:
notes.en: [I meant land suitable for orchards, not land that has trees in it.]

messages.text: When discussing a consecrated ancestral field the Torah states: “An area fit for sowing” (Leviticus 27:16). I have derived only an area fit for sowing; from where do I derive that the same is true for a field of vines and a field of reeds and a field of trees?
messages.lead: Rav Naḥman raised another objection to Rav Huna from a baraita:

notes.he: נפדה בנ' שקלים אלא בית זרע שראוי לזריעה:
notes.en: I have: [derived that it is] redeemed for fifty shekels only for an area of sowing that is suitable for sowing.

messages.text: The verse states: “And if a man shall consecrate to the Lord part of the field of his possession, then your valuation shall be according to an area fit for sowing; the sowing of a ḥomer of barley shall be valued at fifty silver shekels” (Leviticus 27:16). The word “field” teaches that this halakha applies in any case, regardless of the type of field.

verse.he: וְאִם ׀ מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ לְפִי זַרְעוֹ זֶרַע חֹמֶר שְׂעֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף׃
verse.en: If anyone consecrates to GOD a land-holding, its assessment shall be in accordance with its seed requirement: fifty shekels of silver to a ḥomer of barley seed.

notes.he: כלומר שיפדה את השדה ואין צריך לפדות את האילנות:
notes.en: [The verse states] “field,” in any case: that is, that he redeems the field and need not redeem the trees.

messages.text: It can be inferred from here that if one consecrates an orchard, the redemption of the trees is not valued separately from the land.
@Rav Naḥman Here too, the baraita means that he first redeems the trees and afterward redeems the field, according to the formula of the Torah.

notes.he: האילנות בשויהן וחוזר ופודה קרקע. ושדה מ"מ דקאמר לא קאי אלא אקרקע:
notes.en: He redeems: the trees at their value, and then he redeems the land as well. And “field, in any case,” which it says, refers only to the land.

notes.he: כלומר שלאחר שפדה השדה פודה את האילנות]:
notes.en: [Here too, he redeems and redeems again: that is, after he has redeemed the field, he redeems the trees.]

messages.text: If one consecrated three trees in a field where ten trees are planted in an area required for sowing one se’a of seed [beit se’a], he has consecrated not only those trees, but also the land and the young trees between them.
messages.lead: Rav Naḥman again raised an objection to Rav Huna from a baraita:

notes.he: נטועין ומפוזרין כסדרן ממטע עשרה לבית סאה שאם היו עשרה מפוזרין כדרך אלו היו מחזיקין בית סאה זו היא דין נטיעת אילנות וכל קרקע שביניהם צריך להם לפיכך אם הקדישו ה"ז הקדיש קרקע שבניהם וכל אילנות קטנים שביניהם:
notes.en: He consecrated three trees: planted and spread out in their proper order, at the planting density of ten to a beit se’a; that is, if ten were spread out the way these are, they would take up this beit se’a. This is the rule for planting trees, and all the land between them is needed for them. Therefore, if he consecrated them, he has consecrated the land between them and all the small trees between them.

notes.dh: הקדיש שלשה אילנות ממטע עשרה לבית סאה
notes.he: והנך אילנות בנטיעות איירי דאילו גדולים בשלשה [אילנות] לבית סאה סגי:
notes.en: He consecrated three trees of a planting of ten to a beit se’a: these trees are saplings, for if they were grown trees, three [trees] to a beit se’a would suffice.

notes.he: כלומר שישנן נטועין [בשוה] בתוך בית סאה הרי זה הקדיש את הקרקע אגב האילנות אע"ג שלא הזכיר את הקרקע דבטילה היא (אגב) לגבי האילנות [ואת האילנות שביניהם אילנות קטנים שעלו בין אותן אילנות]. פחות מיכן או יתר מכן שנטועין אותן י' אילנות בפחות מבית סאה או מפוזרין ביותר מבית סאה דבטלו מתורת אילנות:
notes.en: Of a planting of ten to a beit se’a: that is, they are planted [evenly] within a beit se’a. He has consecrated the land along with the trees, even though he did not mention the land, because it is subordinate to the trees, [and the trees between them: small trees that came up between those trees]. Less than that or more than that: those ten trees are planted in less than a beit se’a, or spread over more than a beit se’a, for they have lost the status of [a planting of] trees.

messages.text: Therefore, if this is his ancestral field, when he redeems it, he redeems the land and everything contained within it according to the standard rate established by the Torah, where an area required for the sowing of a kor of barley seed is redeemed for fifty silver shekels.

But if the ratio of land to trees was less than that, i.e., the trees were planted more densely, or if the ratio of land to trees was more than that, i.e., the trees were planted less densely, or if he consecrated each of the trees separately, one after the other, this person has consecrated neither the land nor the young trees between them. Therefore, when he redeems, he redeems the trees in accordance with their worth.

notes.he: אם נטועין בפחות ממטע עשרה לבית סאה או ביותר מיכן אין זה סדר נטיעת אילנות ולא הקדיש אלא אילנות וכשהוא פודן פודה בשויהן:
notes.en: Less than that: if they are planted at less than the density of ten to a beit se’a, or more than that, this is not the order of planting trees, and he consecrated only the trees; and when he redeems them, he redeems them at their value.

notes.he: לא קנה הקדש קרקע שאין קנין קרקע אלא לג' אילנות כדאמר בבבא בתרא:
notes.en: One after the other: the Temple treasury did not acquire land, for there is acquisition of land only with three trees [acquired together], as it says in Bava Batra.

notes.dh: פחות מכאן או יתר על כן לא הקדיש את הקרקעות
notes.he: ממטע עשרה לבית סאה מגיע לכל אילן ואילן ר"נ אמות ותימה דבפרק המוכר [את] הספינה (ב"ב דף פב.) תניא הקונה שלשה אילנות והם מד' אמות עד ט"ז קנה תחתיהן וביניהן וצידיהן כמלא אורה וסלו אלמא לא חשבינן להו כרצופין כשאין בין זה לזה כי אם ח' אמות על ח' אמות בריבוע דהיינו ס"ד אמות לכל אחד ואית ליה קרקע בהכי והכא אמרי' דפחות מר"נ אמות לא הקדיש הקרקע ואור"י דיש חילוק בין מוכר למקדיש במוכר לא בעינן כולי האי מיהו תימה דהכא אמרי' דיתר על כן אין לו קרקע וגבי מוכר אמרי' עד ט"ז אמות על ט"ז אמות דהיינו רנ"ו ולא חשבינן להו כמפוזרים יותר מדאי ויש להו קרקע וצ"ל דהני ט"ז אמות דגבי מכירה מיירי בעיגולא והריבוע יתר על העיגול רביע נמצא דגבי מכירה לא בעינן כולי האי כמו מקדיש והקשה רבינו שמואל בבבא בתרא מהא דתניא בתוספתא דאין חילוק בין מוכר למקדיש לדין זה לקנות קרקע ותירץ דתנאי היא מיהו תימה דר' שמעון אית ליה התם דח' אמות בין זה לזה לא חשיב יותר מדאי אף לענין הקדש וברייתא דהכא במטע עשרה לבית סאה מוקי לה הכא בסמוך כר' שמעון וי"ל דלא מוקי כר' שמעון כ"א מדין דמקדיש בעין רעה מקדיש אבל מדין שיעור נטיעת האילנות לא הוי כר' שמעון:
notes.en: In brief: [On “less than that or more than that, he did not consecrate the land.”] At ten to a beit se’a, each tree has 250 square cubits. Tosafot ask from Bava Batra 82a (HaMokher et HaSefina): one who buys three trees standing from four to sixteen cubits apart acquires the land beneath them, between them and beside them, as far as a picker with his basket; so trees eight by eight cubits apart (64 square cubits each) are not too close, yet here less than 250 means no land. The Ri answers that a seller differs from one who consecrates, and a sale needs less. They ask further: here more than 250 means no land, while in a sale trees up to sixteen by sixteen cubits apart (256) are not too spread out; they answer that the sixteen cubits of a sale are measured as a circle, and a square exceeds a circle by a quarter, so a sale still needs less than consecration. Rabbeinu Shmuel in Bava Batra asked from a Tosefta that seller and consecrator do not differ in this, and answered that it is a dispute of tanna’im. A last difficulty: Rabbi Shimon holds there that eight cubits between trees is not too far even for consecration, yet the Gemara soon sets this baraita of ten to a beit se’a as Rabbi Shimon. They answer that it is set as Rabbi Shimon only for the rule that one consecrates sparingly, not for the measure of planting. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: לאילנות הרי זה לא הקדיש (אלא) את הקרקע:
notes.en: Or if he consecrated them one after the other: the trees; he has not consecrated the land.

messages.text: And moreover, even if one consecrated its trees when they are planted more densely, or less densely, or one after the other, and then afterward he consecrated the land, so that at this point everything belongs to the Temple treasury, when he redeems them, he redeems the trees separately in accordance with their worth, and afterward he redeems the land according to the standard rate, where an area required for the sowing of a ḥomer, i.e., a kor, of barley seed is redeemed for fifty silver shekels.

notes.he: ולא אלו בלבד נפדין בשויהן שאין עמהן הקדש קרקע כלל:
notes.en: And not only that: and not only are these redeemed at their value, where there is no consecration of land with them at all.

notes.he: שאינן נטועים כסדר:
notes.en: But even if he consecrated the trees: that are not planted in order.

notes.he: דאיכא למימר ליפרקו אגב ארעייהו אפי' הכי הואיל ולא קדשו יחד פודה אילנות בשויהן והקרקע נפדית בית זרע נ' שקלים:
notes.en: And afterward he consecrated land: where one could say, let them be redeemed along with their land; even so, since they were not consecrated together, he redeems the trees at their value, and the land is redeemed at fifty shekels for an area of sowing.

messages.text: And if you would say that here too, in the first part of the baraita, it means that he redeems the field and afterward redeems the trees, from the fact that the latter clause of the baraita states that he redeems and afterward redeems, by inference the first clause is not referring to a case where he redeems the field and afterward redeems the trees.

notes.he: מרישא דהיכא דהקדישן יחד נפדין אגב קרקע:
notes.en: A refutation of Rav Huna: from the first clause, where, when he consecrated them together, they are redeemed along with the land. [Rashi’s heading reads “a refutation of Rav Huna,” words not in the printed Gemara here.]

notes.dh: אלא (א"כ) [אפי'] הקדיש בפירוש הקרקע וכשהוא פודה וכו'
notes.he: וקא פריך מרישא דברייתא:
notes.en: But [even if] he explicitly consecrated the land, and when he redeems etc. And he raises the challenge from the first clause of the baraita.

messages.text: Rather, in accordance with whose opinion is this baraita? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who says that when one consecrates, he consecrates sparingly. As it is taught in a baraita:
One who consecrates a field has consecrated all of it.

notes.he: כל אשר בתוכה:
notes.en: Has consecrated all of it: everything in it.

messages.text: He only consecrated a grafted carob tree and a sycamore stump.

notes.he: אילנות שבה:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says, he did not consecrate: the trees in it.

notes.he: שהם זקנים וגדולים מאד ויונקים משדה הקדש טפי משאר אילנות והכי מפורש בב"ב. סדן [השקמה] דדרך שקמין לקוץ אותם כדי שיגדלו בעובי וקודם שנקצץ קרי ליה בתולת שקמה ולאחר קציצה קרי ליה סדן השקמה הכי תניא במס' נדה (דף ח:):
notes.en: Except a grafted carob and a sycamore stump: for they are old and very large and draw from the consecrated field more than other trees; and so it is explained in Bava Batra. Sycamore stump [sadan hashikma]: it is the way of sycamores to be cut so that they grow thicker; before it is cut it is called a “virgin sycamore,” and after the cutting it is called a sycamore stump. So it is taught in tractate Niddah (8b).

notes.dh: ר' שמעון אומר לא הקדיש אלא את החרוב כו' דדבר חשוב הן דקא ינקי משדה הקדש
notes.he: אבל לא שאר האילנות דמקדיש בעין רעה מקדיש:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says: He consecrated only the carob etc.: for they are significant, since they draw from the consecrated field; but not the other trees, for one who consecrates, consecrates sparingly.

messages.text: If the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, say the latter clause: And moreover, even if one consecrates its trees and then afterward he consecrated the land, when he redeems them he redeems the trees separately in accordance with their worth, and afterward he redeems the land according to the standard rate, where an area required for the sowing of a ḥomer of barley seed is redeemed for fifty silver shekels.
messages.quote: And moreover, even if one consecrated its trees … and then afterward he consecrated the land

notes.dh: הקדיש את האילנות ואח"כ הקדיש הקרקע
notes.he: אע"פ שנטועין עשרה בבית סאה ובזה אחר זה הקדיש (שדה ואת האילנות כשהוא פודה כו' בשויהן) [פודה את האילנות בשוויהן וחוזר כו':
notes.en: He consecrated the trees and afterward consecrated the land: even though they are planted ten to a beit se’a, and he consecrated one after the other, [he redeems the trees at their value and then redeems again, etc.].

messages.text: And if the baraita is according to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, let one follow the status of the field at the time of its redemption, and let the trees be redeemed along with their land, as at the time of its redemption both the trees and the land are consecrated. As we have heard that Rabbi Shimon follows the time of the redemption, i.e., he determines the price at which a field is redeemed based on the time it is being redeemed.

notes.he: והואיל ובשעת פדיון יש קרקע עם האילנות:
notes.en: Let one follow the redemption: and since at the time of redemption there is land with the trees.

notes.he: ואע"ג דבשעת הקדש הקדישן בפני עצמם:
notes.en: Let them be redeemed along with their land: even though at the time of consecration he consecrated them by themselves.

notes.he: הואיל ובשעת פדיון ישנה לקרקע מקודשת עם האילנות ונפרקו אגב ארעייהו:
notes.en: [Let one follow] the redemption: since at the time of redemption the land is consecrated together with the trees, let them be redeemed along with their land.

messages.text: From where is it derived with regard to one who purchases a field from his father and consecrated it, and afterward his father dies, which means that the field would now be his as an inheritance, from where is it derived that it should be considered before him as an ancestral field, rather than a field that he purchased, with respect to its redemption? The verse states with regard to a field that was purchased: “And if he sanctifies to the Lord a field that he has bought, which is not of his ancestral fields” (Leviticus 27:22).

verse.he: וְאִם אֶת־שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: If one consecrates to GOD land that was purchased, which is not one’s land-holding,

notes.he: אע"ג דבשעת הקדש הואי שדה מקנה הואיל ולאחר שמת אביו הוי שדה אחוזה:
notes.en: And he consecrated it and afterward his father died: even though at the time of consecration it was a purchased field, since after his father died it is an ancestral field.

notes.he: ונפדית בחמשים שקלים ולא בשויה:
notes.en: From where that it should be before him as an ancestral field: and be redeemed for fifty shekels and not at its value.

notes.he: דבשעת הקדש היתה שדה מקנה:
notes.en: From where with regard to one who purchases a field from his father and consecrated it: for at the time of consecration it was a purchased field.

notes.he: והיה ראוי לירש אותה שדה אם לא קנאה:
notes.en: And afterward his father died: and he would have been fit to inherit that field had he not bought it.

notes.he: עכשיו בשעת פדיון:
notes.en: From where that it should be before him: now, at the time of redemption.

notes.he: ויפדה בית זרע חומר שעורים בנ' שקל כסף:
notes.en: As an ancestral field: and he redeems an area for sowing a ḥomer of barley for fifty silver shekels.

messages.text: The verse speaks specifically of a field that is not fit at the time of its consecration to be an ancestral field, i.e., one that he could never have inherited in the future. This specification excludes this field that was fit to be an ancestral field from this halakha, since eventually it would have become his through inheritance, even had he not purchased it. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon.

notes.dh: תלמוד לומר וכו' שדה שאינה ראויה להיות שדה אחוזה
notes.he: יש לה דין שדה מקנה לפדות בשוויה יצתה זו כו':
notes.en: The verse states etc.: a field that is not fit to be an ancestral field has the law of a purchased field, to be redeemed at its value; this one is excluded etc.

notes.he: ת"ל ואם את שדה מקנתו וגו' אלמא אזיל רבי שמעון בתר פדיון אע"ג דלא הויא שדה אחוזה בשעה שהקדישה אלא בשעת פדיון אזלינן בתר השתא:
notes.en: The verse states: “And if a field that he has bought” etc. Evidently Rabbi Shimon follows the redemption: even though it was not an ancestral field when he consecrated it, but [it is one] at the time of redemption, we go by the present.

messages.text: From where is it derived that in a case of one who purchases a field from his father and his father dies, and only afterward he consecrated the field, from where is it derived that it should be considered before him like an ancestral field?
messages.lead: The baraita continues: Rabbi Meir learns a different halakha from this verse and says:

notes.he: דבשעת הקדש הויא שדה אחוזה אבל הקדישה ואח"כ מת אביו אינה אלא כשדה מקנה:
notes.en: And afterward he consecrated it: for at the time of consecration it is an ancestral field; but if he consecrated it and afterward his father died, it is only like a purchased field.

notes.he: דבין בשעת הקדש ובין בשעת פדיון הוי שדה אחוזה:
notes.en: And his father died and afterward he consecrated it: for both at the time of consecration and at the time of redemption it is an ancestral field.

messages.text: The verse states with regard to a purchased field: “And if he sanctifies to the Lord a field that he has bought, which is not of his ancestral field” (Leviticus 27:22). The verse is referring specifically to a field that is not an ancestral field at the time of its consecration. This requirement excludes this field, as currently, after the death of the father, it is an ancestral field.

verse.he: וְאִם אֶת־שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: If one consecrates to GOD land that was purchased, which is not one’s land-holding,

messages.text: That is the opinion of Rabbi Meir, whereas according to Rabbi Yehuda and according to Rabbi Shimon it is considered an ancestral field even if he consecrated the field and afterward his father dies. What is the reason for this opinion?

If you suggest it is due to the verse, that cannot be, as the verse comes to teach the halakha that was stated in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, i.e., it is referring to a case where the father died before he consecrated the field, as Rabbi Meir explained.

notes.he: דאשר לא משדה אחוזתו דלמא לאו למעוטי הקדישה ואח"כ מת אביו אלא למעוטי מת אביו ואח"כ הקדישה וכדדריש ליה רבי מאיר:
notes.en: If because of the verse: “which is not of his ancestral field”; perhaps it does not come to exclude a case where he consecrated it and afterward his father died, but rather to exclude a case where his father died and afterward he consecrated it, as Rabbi Meir expounds it.

notes.he: אי קא סברת דמשום קרא דקא דרשי שדה שאינה ראויה ההוא] קרא לכדר' מאיר הוא דאתא דלדידיה מיסתבר טפי. [אלא לאו דאזיל בתר פדיון]:
notes.en: [What is the reason? If you think it is because of the verse that they expound, “a field that is not fit,” that] verse comes for Rabbi Meir’s ruling, for according to him it is more reasonable. [Rather, is it not that he follows the redemption?]

messages.text: Rather, is it not due to the fact that he follows the status of the field at the time of the redemption? Since the father died before the son redeemed the field it is considered an ancestral field in the possession of the Temple treasury.

notes.he: וכיון דבשעת פדיון מת אביו הויא לה שדה אחוזה:
notes.en: The redemption: and since by the time of redemption his father had died, it has become an ancestral field.

messages.text: Similarly, if one first consecrates the trees and afterward the field, he should redeem them both together, since at the time of the redemption they are both consecrated. Since this ruling is not in accordance with the baraita that states that the trees and field are redeemed separately, evidently the baraita cannot be in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon.

This source does not contradict Rav Huna’s claim that the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon. The reason is that Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon do not, in fact, maintain that one follows the status of the field at the time of the redemption. Rather, they found a verse and expounded it.

notes.he: אמר רב נחמן בר יצחק לעולם רבי יהודה ורבי שמעון בעלמא לא אזלי בתר פדיון והכא גבי לוקח שדה מאביו מ"ט אזלי בתר פדיון קרא אשכחו ודרוש מקרא יתירא דא"כ דלא אזלינן בתר פדיון ליכתוב אם [את] שדה מקנתו אשר לא אחוזתו אי נמי [אשר לא] שדה אחוזתו מאי משדה ש"מ שאינה ראויה להיות כו':
notes.en: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Actually, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon do not generally follow the redemption. And here, with one who purchases a field from his father, why do they follow the redemption? They found a verse and expounded it, from a superfluous verse: for if so, that we do not follow the redemption, let it write “a field that he has bought, which is not his ancestral” or “[which is not an] ancestral field”; what is “of his field”? Learn from this: [a field] that is not fit to be etc.

messages.text: If so, that when one consecrated the field and his father died afterward, it is not considered an ancestral field, let the Merciful One write in the Torah: And if he sanctifies to the Lord a field that he has bought, which is not his ancestral, i.e., the verse could have omitted the repetition of the phrase “of his field.”

notes.he: דלכדר' מאיר הוא דאתא לכתוב רחמנא וכו':
notes.en: If so: that it comes for Rabbi Meir’s ruling, let the Merciful One write etc.

messages.text: What does the Torah mean by stressing “of his field”? This teaches that only a field that is not fit to be an ancestral field at the time he consecrated it is redeemed for its value. But if he consecrated a field that he would inherit in the future, it is redeemed in the manner of an ancestral field.
If one consecrated fields that are rocky [terashin] and unsuitable for planting, he redeems them by their value, not as ancestral fields.

notes.he: ואע"ג דאחוזה נינהו:
notes.en: He redeems them at their value: even though they are ancestral.

notes.he: שדה מליאה סלעים שאינה ראויה לזרע:
notes.en: Rocky ground [terashin]: a field full of rocks that is not suitable for sowing.

messages.text: What is the reason? The Merciful One states that one redeems an area fit for sowing of a ḥomer of barley seed for fifty silver shekels (see Leviticus 27:16), and these fields are not fit for sowing.
But if he did not redeem these fields before the Jubilee Year, they go to the priests in the Jubilee Year, like ancestral fields.

notes.he: ומכרם גזבר לאחר:
notes.en: He did not redeem them: and the treasurer sold them to another.

notes.he: כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״א) ואם לא יגאל וגו' וכתיב והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל וגו':
notes.en: They go out to the priests in the Jubilee: as it is written: “And if he will not redeem” etc. (Leviticus 27:20), and it is written: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee” etc. (Leviticus 27:21).

messages.text: What is the reason? The Merciful One states: “And if he will not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed anymore. But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy to the Lord, as a field devoted; it shall belong to the priest” (Leviticus 27:20–21). This indicates that any kind of ancestral field at all, regardless of quality, goes to the priests if it is not redeemed by the Jubilee Year.

verse.he: וְאִם־לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה וְאִם־מָכַר אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד׃ וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: But if the one [who consecrated it] did not redeem the land, and the land was sold to another party, it shall no longer be redeemable: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.he: והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל וגו' (שם):
notes.en: The Merciful One said “field”: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee” etc. (ibid.).

notes.he: שדה כל דהו בין ראוי לזרע בין אין ראוי לזרע:
notes.en: Field, of any kind: whether suitable for sowing or not suitable for sowing.

messages.text: If one sold fields that are rocky and unsuitable for planting, they may be redeemed from the purchaser in even less than two years, despite the fact that normally land must be left in the hands of the purchaser for at least two years (see 29b), as derived from the plural term “years of the crops” cited below.

notes.he: ואע"ג דמוכר קרקע לחבירו אין רשאי לגאול עד שתהא שתי שנים ביד הלוקח כדכתיב (שם כה) במספר שני תבואות וגו':
notes.en: Less than two years: even though one who sells land to another may not redeem it until it has been two years in the hand of the purchaser, as it is written: “According to the number of years of the crops” etc. (Leviticus 25:15).

notes.he: דאמרי' לקמן המוכר [שדהו] בשעת היובל אינו מותר לגאול פחות מב' שנים שנאמר במספר שני תבואות ימכר לך:
notes.en: They may be redeemed in less than two years: for we say below that one who sells [his field] while the Jubilee is in force may not redeem it in less than two years, as it is stated: “According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you” (Leviticus 25:15).

messages.text: What is the reason? The Merciful One states: “According to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy from your neighbor, and according to the number of years of the crops he shall sell it to you” (Leviticus 25:15), and these rocky fields are not fit for crops.

verse.he: בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל תִּקְנֶה מֵאֵת עֲמִיתֶךָ בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי־תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר־לָךְ׃
verse.en: In buying from your neighbor, you shall deduct only for the number of years since the jubilee; and in selling to you, you shall be charged only for the remaining crop years:

messages.text: But if he did not redeem them from the purchaser, they return to the owner in the Jubilee Year, like ancestral fields.

What is the reason? The Merciful One states: “Then let him count the years of its sale, and restore the extra to the man to whom he sold it; and it shall return to its ancestral heritage” (Leviticus 25:27), and this rocky field is also part of his ancestral heritage.

verse.he: וְחִשַּׁב אֶת־שְׁנֵי מִמְכָּרוֹ וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת־הָעֹדֵף לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר מָכַר־לוֹ וְשָׁב לַאֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: the years since its sale shall be computed and the difference shall be refunded to the party to whom it was sold, so that [the seller] returns to their holding.

notes.he: ואחוזתו היא כמות שהיא:
notes.en: “And it shall return to his ancestral holding”: and his ancestral holding is whatever it is.

messages.text: If one consecrated trees in his ancestral field, he redeems them according to their value.

What is the reason? The Merciful One states that one redeems an area fit for sowing of a ḥomer of barley seed for fifty silver shekels. This is referring specifically to land fit for sowing grain, and not trees.
Furthermore, if he did not redeem the trees, they do not go to the priests in the Jubilee Year, unlike an ancestral field.

notes.dh: לא גאלם אין יוצאין לכהנים ביובל
notes.he: אם מכרם גזבר לאחר:
notes.en: He did not redeem them, they do not go out to the priests in the Jubilee: if the treasurer sold them to another.

notes.he: כשדה אחוזה אלא לעולם בעלים רשאין לפדותה:
notes.en: They do not go out to the priests in the Jubilee: like an ancestral field; rather, the owner may always redeem it.

messages.text: The reason is that the Merciful One states: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy to the Lord, as a field devoted; it shall belong to the priest” (Leviticus 27:21). This too is referring specifically to a field, and not trees.

verse.he: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

messages.text: If one sold trees of his ancestral field, they may not be redeemed from the purchaser if less than two years passed.

What is the reason? The Merciful One states: “According to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy it from your neighbor, and according to the number of years of the crops he shall sell it to you” (Leviticus 25:15), and these trees are fit for crops, as they produce fruit.

verse.he: בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל תִּקְנֶה מֵאֵת עֲמִיתֶךָ בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי־תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר־לָךְ׃
verse.en: In buying from your neighbor, you shall deduct only for the number of years since the jubilee; and in selling to you, you shall be charged only for the remaining crop years:

messages.text: But if he did not redeem them from the purchaser, the trees do not return to the owner in the Jubilee Year.

What is the reason? The Merciful One states: “Then let him count the years of its sale, and restore the extra to the man to whom he sold it; and it shall return to its ancestral heritage” (Leviticus 25:27). This includes only land, which remains forever, and not trees, which have a limited lifespan.

verse.he: וְחִשַּׁב אֶת־שְׁנֵי מִמְכָּרוֹ וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת־הָעֹדֵף לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר מָכַר־לוֹ וְשָׁב לַאֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: the years since its sale shall be computed and the difference shall be refunded to the party to whom it was sold, so that [the seller] returns to their holding.

messages.caption: Rav Pappa’s eight rulings: rocky fields and trees, consecrated or sold, and the word in each verse behind them.

messages.text: The Master, i.e., Rav Pappa, says that if one consecrated trees in his ancestral field he redeems them according to their value. Why is that so? But let them be consecrated on account of their land and let them be redeemed on account of their land, according to the valuation of fifty silver shekels for each area required for sowing a kor of barley seed.
messages.quote: If one consecrated trees in his ancestral field, he redeems them according to their value

notes.he: מקום מושב האילן ולהדרו לבעלים אגב ארעייהו אם מכרן והגיע היובל ואמאי אמר מכר אילנות ולא גאלם אין חוזרין לבעלים ביובל:
notes.en: Let them be redeemed along with their land: the place where the tree stands; and let them return to the owner along with their land, if he sold them and the Jubilee arrived. So why did he say: If he sold trees and did not redeem them, they do not return to the owner in the Jubilee?

notes.he: האילנות (שמכר) [שהקדיש] [זרע חומר שעורים בנ' שקל וליהדרו לבעל ביובל אגב ארעייהו היכא דמכר]:
notes.en: Let them be redeemed along with their land: the trees [that he consecrated], [at an area for sowing a ḥomer of barley for fifty shekels; and let them return to the owner in the Jubilee along with their land, where he sold them]. [The editor suggests reading: the trees that he consecrated, to be redeemed by the reckoning of the sowing of a ḥomer of barley, etc.]

messages.text: And if you would say that he consecrated the trees and did not consecrate land, but didn’t the Sages of Neharde’a say: If one sells a date palm to another, the purchaser acquires it from the bottom of the palm until the depths of the earth, i.e., including its land.

notes.he: מקום מושב האילן עד תהומו:
notes.en: From the bottom: the place where the tree stands, down to its depths.

notes.he: שיפוליה שוליו מסביבות שרשיו ולמטה עד התהום:
notes.en: From the bottom to the depths: its bottom is its base around its roots, and downward to the depths.

messages.text: Wasn’t it stated with regard to this ruling that it is referring only to a case where the purchaser comes due to a specific claim that he purchased the land under the date palm. But if he does not claim to have explicitly purchased the land, the seller or the one who consecrates does not intend to include land with the date palm.

notes.he: שטוענו שהזכיר לו שם קרקע:
notes.en: Due to a claim: that he claims that [the seller] mentioned land to him.

notes.he: כשטוען שלקח הקרקע מקום מושב האילן (עצמו) [עמו] וכבר יש לו שני חזקה:
notes.en: [When the Nehardeans said this,] it was where he comes due to a claim: when he claims that he bought the land, the place where the tree stands, [with it], and he already has the years of presumptive ownership.

messages.text: § The Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: And with regard to a purchased field that one consecrates, he gives its value

messages.text: The verse states: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the worth of your valuation until the Jubilee Year; and he shall give your valuation in that day, as a holy thing to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:23). What does this word “worth” come to teach? Since it is stated with regard to an ancestral field: “An area fit for the sowing of a ḥomer of barley seed is redeemed for fifty silver shekels” (Leviticus 27:16), one might have thought that a purchased field is also redeemed using this formula. Therefore, the verse states “worth,” which means the market value of the field.

verse.he: וְחִשַּׁב־לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֵת מִכְסַת הָעֶרְכְּךָ עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנָתַן אֶת־הָעֶרְכְּךָ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: the priest shall compute the proportionate assessment up to the jubilee year, and the assessment shall be paid as of that day, a sacred donation to GOD.

notes.he: שדה מקנה כתיב (שם כז) וחשב לו הכהן את מכסת הערכך:
notes.en: A purchased field: it is written: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the worth of your valuation” (Leviticus 27:23).

notes.he: בגאולת שדה אחוזה זרע חומר שעורים:
notes.en: Since it is stated: in the redemption of an ancestral field, “the sowing of a ḥomer of barley.”

notes.he: מנין דמיו דהיינו שויין:
notes.en: The verse states “worth [mikhsat]”: the count of its money, that is, its value.

notes.he: דכתיב גבי מקנה דכתיב וחשב לו הכהן את מכסת הערכך] ת"ל מכסת ואין מכסת אלא דמים דמי שוויו כדאמרן לקמן:
notes.en: [What does “worth [mikhsat]” teach? For it is written with a purchased field: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the worth of your valuation.”] The verse states “worth,” and “worth” means nothing but money, the money of its value, as we said below.

messages.text: It is stated here, with regard to purchased fields: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the worth of your valuation until the Jubilee Year; and he shall give your valuation in that day, as a holy thing to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:23). And it is stated there, with regard to an ancestral field: “But if he sanctifies his field after the Jubilee, then the priest shall reckon for him the money according to the years that remain until the Jubilee Year, and it shall be deducted from your valuation” (Leviticus 27:18).

verse.he: וְאִם־אַחַר הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ וְחִשַּׁב־לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף עַל־פִּי הַשָּׁנִים הַנּוֹתָרֹת עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנִגְרַע מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verse.en: But if the land is consecrated after the jubilee, the priest shall compute the price according to the years that are left until the jubilee year, and its assessment shall be so reduced;

notes.he: בשדה מקנה ולהלן בשדה אחוזה:
notes.en: It is stated here: with a purchased field; and there: with an ancestral field.

messages.text: Just as there, in the case of an ancestral field, it is referring to a fixed amount, so too here, with regard to a purchased field, it means a fixed amount.

notes.he: חמשים כסף:
notes.en: A fixed amount: fifty [shekels of] silver.

notes.he: בשדה אחוזה וחשב לו הכהן את הכסף על פי השנים וכו' מה להלן דבר קצוב זרע חומר שעורים בנ' שקל אף כאן נמי:
notes.en: [It is stated here “shall reckon,” and it is stated there, with an ancestral field: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the money according to the years” etc. Just as there it is a fixed amount, the sowing of a ḥomer of barley for fifty shekels, so too here.]

messages.text: Do the Rabbis, who disagree with Rabbi Eliezer, accept that one derives the verbal analogy of “shall reckon,” but they use it to derive that one who redeems a consecrated purchased field must also add one-fifth? Or perhaps they do not accept the verbal analogy at all, and they do not hold that one who redeems a purchased field must add one-fifth?
messages.lead: A dilemma was raised before the students:

notes.dh: מי אית להו הך גזירה שוה
notes.he: דוחשב ומפקי ליה לחומש למילף חומש אשדה מקנה משדה אחוזה:
notes.en: Do they accept this verbal analogy: of “shall reckon,” and use it for the fifth, to derive a fifth for a purchased field from an ancestral field?

notes.dh: איבעיא להו לרבנן אית להו גז"ש ומפקין ליה לחומש או דלמא כו'
notes.he: קשה לרבינו אלחנן אמאי לא נילף מינהון ג"ש נהי דבנין אב לא ילפינן מינייהו מ"מ ג"ש נילף מינייהו ונראה לר' מדאיצטריך למיכתב חומש גבי מקדיש שדה אחוזה וגבי מקדיש את ביתו ומצינו למילף חד מחבריה בג"ש ולא ילפינן אלא כתב חומש לכל חד וחד ש"מ שני כתובין הבאים כאחד ולא ילפינן מינייהו בעלמא אפילו בג"ש:
notes.en: A dilemma was raised: do the Rabbis accept the verbal analogy and use it for the fifth, or perhaps etc.: Rabbeinu Elḥanan found it difficult: why not derive a verbal analogy from them? Granted that we do not derive a paradigm [binyan av] from them, nevertheless let us derive a verbal analogy from them. And it seems to our teacher [the text has only “R.”]: since it was necessary to write a fifth for one who consecrates an ancestral field and for one who consecrates his house, and we could have derived one from the other by a verbal analogy, yet we do not derive it, but [the Torah] wrote a fifth for each one, learn from this that they are two verses that come as one, and we do not derive from them elsewhere, even by a verbal analogy.

notes.he: לרבנן דאמרי בשדה מקנה נותן את שוויו אית להו גזרה שוה וחשב וחשב ומפקי ליה לג"ש לחומש דמה שדה אחוזה מוסיף חומש אף שדה מקנה מוסיף חומש:
notes.en: According to the Rabbis, who say that with a purchased field one gives its value: do they accept the verbal analogy “shall reckon”–“shall reckon,” and use the verbal analogy for the fifth: just as with an ancestral field one adds a fifth, so with a purchased field one adds a fifth?

notes.dh: או דלמא לית להו ג"ש ולית להו חומש
notes.he: בשדה מקנה]:
notes.en: Or perhaps they do not accept the verbal analogy, and they do not hold of a fifth [with a purchased field]?

messages.text: It is reasonable to assume that the Rabbis do not accept the verbal analogy. The reasoning is as follows: From the fact that the Merciful One revealed in the Torah that one must add one-fifth in the case of one who redeems an ancestral field and in the case of one who consecrates his house, these are two verses that come as one, i.e., to teach the same matter.

notes.he: חומש בשדה אחוזה ובמקדיש בית בפרשת בחקתי וחומש דבהמה טמאה וטהורה ומעשר שני נמי התם כתיב:
notes.en: A fifth for an ancestral field and for one who consecrates a house: in the portion of Beḥukkotai; and the fifth for a non-kosher and a kosher animal and for second tithe is also written there.

notes.dh: (לעיל) הוו להו שני כתובין הבאין כאחד
notes.he: וא"ת מה ענין זה לשני כתובין הבאין כאחד כיון דגבי שדה מקנה איכא ג"ש למילף חומש משדה אחוזה וגבי מקדיש בית ליכא ג"ש ושמא הכא דכתיב והעריך גבי מקדיש בית כמאן דכתיב וחשב או שמא י"ל וחשב אין זו ג"ש גמורה אע"ג דקרי ליה הספר ג"ש וה"נ אשכחן בפ"ק דב"ק (דף ו:) גבי נאמר שדה למעלה ונאמר שדה למטה קרי ליה התם ג"ש ואור"י דאינו ג"ש גמורה או שמא י"ל משום דכתיב קודש גבי מקדיש שדה אחוזה וכתיב נמי קודש [גבי] מקדיש בית וקודש קודש ג"ש גמורה היא מש"ה קרי ליה ב' כתובין הבאים כאחד:
notes.en: They are two verses that come as one: And if you say: what does this have to do with two verses that come as one? For with a purchased field there is a verbal analogy to derive a fifth from an ancestral field, but with one who consecrates a house there is no verbal analogy. Perhaps here, since “and he shall value” is written with one who consecrates a house, it is as if “shall reckon” were written. Or perhaps one may say that “shall reckon” is not a complete verbal analogy, even though the book calls it a verbal analogy; and we find the same in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (6b), with “field is stated above and field is stated below,” which is called a verbal analogy there, and the Ri said that it is not a complete verbal analogy. Or perhaps one may say: since “holy” is written with one who consecrates an ancestral field, and “holy” is also written with one who consecrates a house, and “holy”–“holy” is a complete verbal analogy, for this reason it calls them two verses that come as one.

messages.text: And any two verses that come as one do not teach their common aspect, in this case, adding one-fifth, to apply to other cases. Therefore, it can be assumed that the Rabbis maintain that one who redeems his purchased field does not have to pay an additional fifth.

And even according to the one who says that two verses that come as one do teach their common aspect, from the fact that the Merciful One revealed in the Torah that one must add one-fifth when he redeems his second tithe, and when he redeems his kosher animal that he consecrated and became blemished, and when he redeems his non-kosher animal that he consecrated, these are many verses that come at one, and everyone agrees that multiple verses do not teach their common aspect to other cases.

notes.he: כתובים הבאין כאחד ואין מלמדין:
notes.en: They are many: verses that come as one, and they do not teach.

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with the ruling of Rava, but not for his reason.

notes.he: דאין חומש בשדה מקנה:
notes.en: It is taught in accordance with Rava: that there is no fifth for a purchased field.

notes.he: דאילו טעמא דרבא מדגלי חומש בכל הנך דוכתי וטעמא דברייתא מדהיקישו לערכין לאדם שהעריך עצמו או חבירו:
notes.en: But not for his reason: for Rava’s reason is from the fact that [the Torah] revealed a fifth in all these places, and the baraita’s reason is that it juxtaposed it to valuations, of a person who valuated himself or another.

messages.text: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the worth of your valuation until the Jubilee Year; and he shall give your valuation in that day, as a holy thing to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:23). The verse juxtaposes this estimation to fixed valuations. Just as with regard to fixed valuations one does not add one-fifth, so too when redeeming a purchased field one does not add one-fifth.

verse.he: וְחִשַּׁב־לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֵת מִכְסַת הָעֶרְכְּךָ עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנָתַן אֶת־הָעֶרְכְּךָ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: the priest shall compute the proportionate assessment up to the jubilee year, and the assessment shall be paid as of that day, a sacred donation to GOD.

notes.he: כלומר דנותן את שוויו]:
notes.en: [“Worth [mikhsat]” means nothing but money: that is, he gives its value.] [The editor notes that this is Rabbeinu Gershom’s reading of the baraita here.]

notes.he: שהיה נותן בישרות נפש אחד מחמש המאות ולא היה מפסיד:
notes.en: “And levy a tribute [mekhes] to the Lord” (Numbers 31:28): that he would fairly give one soul out of five hundred, and would not lose by it.

notes.he: ערכי אדם [אין מוסיף חומש:
notes.en: Just as valuations: valuations of a person, [one does not add a fifth].

messages.text: Mishna
There are halakhot with regard to a forewarned ox that killed a Canaanite slave that are lenient and others that are stringent; how so?

Both in the case of an ox that killed the most attractive among the slaves, whose value is great, and likewise in the case of one that killed the most unsightly among the slaves, whose value is minimal, its owner gives payment of thirty sela, the fine stated in the Torah (Exodus 21:32), to the owner of the slave.

verse.he: אִם־עֶבֶד יִגַּח הַשּׁוֹר אוֹ אָמָה כֶּסֶף ׀ שְׁלֹשִׁים שְׁקָלִים יִתֵּן לַאדֹנָיו וְהַשּׁוֹר יִסָּקֵל׃ {ס}
verse.en: But if the ox gores a slave, male or female, [its owner] shall pay thirty shekels of silver to the master, and the ox shall be stoned.

messages.text: If the ox killed a freeman, its owner gives his price as payment to his heirs. This sum can be more or less than thirty shekels.

notes.dh: מתני' המית בן חורין נותן שויו
notes.he: דכתיב במועד (שמות כ״א:ל׳) אם כופר יושת עליו וגו' ותניא בב"ק (דף מ.) ונתן פדיון נפשו דמי ניזק:
notes.en: Mishna. Killed a freeman, he gives his value: as it is written with regard to a forewarned ox: “If a ransom be laid on him” etc. (Exodus 21:30), and it is taught in Bava Kamma (40a): “Then he shall give for the redemption of his life”: the value of the injured party.

notes.dh: המית בן חורין] נותן את שוויו
notes.he: של בעל השור והיינו כופר (ואת) [ואם תימצא] לומר שוויו של מומת היינו דמים כדאמרינן בבבא קמא:
notes.en: [Killed a freeman,] he gives his value: [the value] of the owner of the ox, and that is the ransom; [and if you should] say the value of the one killed, that is money, as we say in Bava Kamma.

messages.text: If the ox injured this slave or that freeman, he gives payment of the full cost of the damage as compensation.

notes.he: בין בעבד בין בבן חורין ולא המיתו משלם נזק שלם:
notes.en: Injured this one or that one: whether a slave or a freeman, and did not kill him; he pays full damage.

notes.he: שאם חבל שור המועד בין בעבד בין בבן חורין משלם נזק שלם:
notes.en: Injured this one or that one: if a forewarned ox injured either a slave or a freeman, he pays full damage.

messages.text: Gemara

As the mishna first specifies that it is speaking of a forewarned ox, this indicates that with regard to a forewarned ox that injured a freeman, yes, one is liable for full payment, but with regard to an innocuous ox that injured a freeman one does not make full restitution, but pays only half the value of the victim.
messages.quote: with regard to a forewarned ox

notes.he: אסיפא קאי דקתני חבל בזה ובזה כו' דרישא פשיטא לן דקנס דעבד לא שייך בתם דכתיב בתם ובעל השור נקי ואמרי' בב"ק בפ' שור שנגח ארבעה וחמשה (דף מב.) נקי מדמי עבד וקתני נמי המית בן חורין נותן שויו ודמי כופר לא שייך בתם דהתם נמי אמרינן נקי מחצי כופר:
notes.en: Gemara. With a forewarned ox, yes; with an innocuous ox, no: this refers to the latter clause, which teaches: “injured this one or that one” etc. For the first clause is obvious to us: the fine for a slave does not apply to an innocuous ox, as it is written with regard to an innocuous ox: “But the owner of the ox shall be clear” (Exodus 21:28), and we say in Bava Kamma, in the chapter Shor SheNagaḥ Arba’a VeḤamisha (42a): clear of the payment for a slave. And it also teaches: “killed a freeman, he gives his value,” and ransom does not apply to an innocuous ox, for there too we say: clear of half the ransom.

notes.dh: במועד אין בתם לא לימא מתני' דלא כרבי עקיבא כו'
notes.he: אסיפא דסיפא קאי דקתני חבל בזה ובזה משלם נזק שלם אבל לא מצי למימר דקאי אהמית העבד ולא אהמית בן חורין דבהא לא פליג רבי עקיבא דתם אינו משלם לא כופר ולא שלשים של עבד כדאיתא בב"ק בפ' שור שנגח ד' וה' (בבא קמא דף מב:):
notes.en: With a forewarned ox, yes; with an innocuous, no; let us say the mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva etc.: this refers to the very last clause, which teaches: “injured this one or that one, he pays full damage.” But one cannot say that it refers to “killed a slave” and “killed a freeman,” for in this Rabbi Akiva does not disagree, that an innocuous ox pays neither ransom nor the thirty of a slave, as stated in Bava Kamma, in the chapter Shor SheNagaḥ Arba’a VeḤamisha (42b).

notes.he: כלומר מועד משלם נזק שלם אם חבל באדם אבל תם לא משלם אלא חצי נזק:
notes.en: With a forewarned ox, yes; with an innocuous ox, no: that is, a forewarned ox pays full damage if it injured a person, but an innocuous one pays only half damage.

messages.text: Let us say that the mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva. As we learned in a mishna (Bava Kamma 33a):

The owner of an innocuous ox that injured a person also pays the full cost of the damage with regard to the difference between the damage the person inflicted on the ox and the damage the ox inflicted on the person.

notes.he: בב"ק בפ' המניח את הכד שני שוורים תמים שחבלו זה בזה כו' ר' עקיבא אומר אף תם שחבל באדם משלם במותר נזק שלם והיינו במותר אם חבל גם האדם בשור ושמו בית דין חבלה שבאדם יותר על חבלה שבשור בעל השור משלם אותו מותר נזק שלם. אלמא תם שחבל באדם משלם נזק שלם:
notes.en: Also an innocuous ox that injured a person etc.: in Bava Kamma, in the chapter HaMani’aḥ et HaKad: two innocuous oxen that injured each other etc.; Rabbi Akiva says: also an innocuous ox that injured a person pays full damage for the excess. That is, for the excess: if the person also injured the ox, and the court assessed the injury to the person as greater than the injury to the ox, the owner of the ox pays that excess as full damage. Evidently an innocuous ox that injured a person pays full damage.

notes.he: מי שחבל יותר באחד:
notes.en: [Pays] for the excess: whoever injured the other more.

messages.text: Evidently, Rabbi Akiva does not distinguish between an innocuous and a forewarned ox in a case where an ox injured a person.
You may even say that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, and explain it as follows: The same is true that even the owner of an innocuous ox must make full restitution,

but since the tanna wants to teach in the first part of the latter clause of the mishna: An ox that killed a slave and an ox that killed a freeman, which you find in the case of forewarned ox but in the case of an innocuous ox you do not find it, as the penalty for killing a person does not apply to an innocuous ox, it is for this reason that the mishna teaches only the case of a forewarned ox.

notes.dh: איידי דבעי למיתני סיפא המית עבד המית בן חורין כו' משום הכי
notes.he: נקט ברישא מועד. והאי דקאמר סיפא לאו סיפא ממש אלא סיפא דרישא היא דמועד ברישא קתני לה:
notes.en: Since it wants to teach in the latter clause: killed a slave, killed a freeman, etc.; for this reason it chose a forewarned ox in the first clause. And what it calls “the latter clause” is not the actual latter clause, but the latter part of the first clause, for the forewarned ox is taught in the first clause.

notes.he: דמשלמי הבעלים כופר:
notes.en: Which you find with a forewarned ox: that the owner pays ransom.

notes.he: דכתיב ובעל השור נקי:
notes.en: With an innocuous ox you do not find it: as it is written: “But the owner of the ox shall be clear” (Exodus 21:28).

messages.text: Mishna
There are halakhot with regard to a rapist and with regard to a seducer that are lenient and others that are stringent; how so?

Both one who raped or seduced a young woman who is the most prominent in the priesthood and one who raped or seduced a young woman who is the lowliest among the Israelites gives the payment of fifty sela, the fine stated in the Torah (see Deuteronomy 22:29).

verse.he: וְנָתַן הָאִישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵב עִמָּהּ לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָ חֲמִשִּׁים כָּסֶף וְלוֹ־תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר עִנָּהּ לֹא־יוּכַל שַׁלְּחָהּ כׇּל־יָמָיו׃ {ס}
verse.en: the man who lay with her shall pay the young woman’s father fifty [shekels of] silver, and she shall be his wife. Because he has violated her, he can never have the right to divorce her.

messages.text: And the payments for humiliation and for degradation resulting from being raped or seduced are assessed differentially; it is all based on the one who humiliates and the one who is humiliated.

notes.he: מפרש בכתובות (ד' מ.) שמין אותה כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בין שפחה בתולה לשפחה בעולה להשיאה לעבדו שיש לו קורת רוח הימנו:
notes.en: Mishna. Degradation: it is explained in Ketubot (40a): one assesses her by how much more a person would be willing to give for a virgin maidservant than for a non-virgin maidservant, to marry her to his slave who has given him satisfaction.

notes.he: ופגם מפרש בכתובות (דף מ:) אומדים כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בשפחה בתולה יותר מבעולה להשיאה לעבדו שעשה לו קורת רוח:
notes.en: Humiliation, all according to the one who humiliates and the one humiliated: and degradation is explained in Ketubot (40b): one estimates how much more a person would be willing to give for a virgin maidservant than for a non-virgin, to marry her to his slave who has given him satisfaction.

notes.he: שאם בייש את אדם חשוב אינו משלם כמו שאם בייש הדיוט אי נמי בייש חשוב משלם יותר משאם בייש הדיוטות:
notes.en: [All according to] the one who humiliates and the one humiliated: for if he humiliated an important person, he does not pay the same as if he humiliated a commoner; alternatively, [where] an important person humiliated, he pays more than [where] commoners humiliated.

messages.caption: The three mishnayot on this daf: what the Torah fixes, whoever the victim, and what is assessed case by case.

messages.text: Gemara

Why must the rapist or seducer also pay for her humiliation and degradation? One can say that the Merciful One states in the verse: “Then the man that lay with her shall give to the young woman’s father fifty shekels of silver” (Deuteronomy 22:29), that he is to pay a total of fifty sela for all matters associated with this act, i.e., the fine, degradation, humiliation, and pain.
messages.quote: the payments for humiliation and for degradation

notes.he: ובושת ופגם לא ליתיב ליה:
notes.en: For all matters: and he should not give her humiliation and degradation.

notes.he: [ואימא אמאי נ' סלע לכולהו מילי לקנס ולבושת ולפגם:
notes.en: [But say: why? Fifty sela for all matters: for the fine, for humiliation and for degradation.]

messages.text: It cannot be that he pays a total of only fifty sela, as people will say: Does it make sense that one who engaged in forced intercourse with, i.e., raped, a daughter of kings pays a sum of fifty sela, when she suffers great humiliation, and one who engaged in forced intercourse with the daughter of ordinary people [hedyotot] also pays fifty sela?

notes.he: בתמיה אבל השתא כי יהיב בושת יש חילוק בין בת מלכים לבת הדיוטות:
notes.en: One who had intercourse with a daughter of commoners etc.: as an exclamation of astonishment. But now, when he gives humiliation, there is a distinction between a daughter of kings and a daughter of commoners.

notes.dh: יאמרו בת מלכים חמשים בת הדיוט חמשים
notes.he: יש תימה קצת דבמשנה תני אחד הגדולה שבכהונה ואחד הקטנה שבישראל נותן חמשים ומאי שנא דהכא מזכיר בגמ' הגדולה בת מלכים ובמשנה תנא גדולה שבכהונה:
notes.en: They will say: a daughter of kings, fifty; a daughter of a commoner, fifty: it is somewhat puzzling, for in the mishna it is taught: both the most prominent in the priesthood and the lowliest among the Israelites, he gives fifty. Why is it different, that here in the Gemara it names the prominent one as a daughter of kings, while the mishna teaches the most prominent in the priesthood?

notes.dh: א"כ יאמרו בעל וכו' מה בין זו לזו
notes.he: אלא ש"מ שמוסיף לבת חשובים בושתה]:
notes.en: [If so, people will say: one who had intercourse etc.; what is the difference between this one and that one? Rather, learn from this that for the daughter of important people he adds her humiliation.]

messages.text: @Rav Zeira If so, the same claim can be applied with regard to a slave killed by an ox. People will also say: Does it make sense that a slave who pierces pearls [margalit] is worth thirty sela, and a slave who performs needlecraft is also worth thirty sela? Nevertheless, the mishna clearly indicates that there is no distinction between the two slaves, as the Torah states a fixed payment.
messages.quote: a daughter of kings pays a sum of fifty sela

notes.dh: אי הכי גבי עבד נמי יאמרו כו'
notes.he: וקי"ל דבין לזה ובין לזה שלשים ותו לא:
notes.en: If so, with a slave too people will say etc. And we hold that for this one and for that one it is thirty and no more.

messages.lead: Rather, Rav Zeira says that there is a different proof:

messages.text: Continues on 15a: Rav Zeira’s second proof, from a young woman forced by two men, one in an atypical manner and one in a typical manner, and Abaye’s answer to it.
